# GitHub Copilot instructions

## TimeLens work log

This standing instruction applies to every user request and logical work chunk, across all local and remote projects and repositories on GitHub and GitLab, including this repository. Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and other agents must follow it without waiting to be reminded. Repository copies must be self-contained so the rule works on another machine or a cloud checkout.

- Before work, call `timelens_get_context` for the user's local today and timezone. Derive a work signature from the concrete deliverable, repository or product surface, named files/tools, and distinctive terms.
- Run at least two narrow `timelens_search_plan_items` searches: one for the strongest distinctive phrase and one for a relevant file, tool, product surface, or project. Expand each search from local today through the prior 3 days, week, month, 3 months, 6 months, year, then all time until a confident match is found. Supplement unclear results with `timelens_search` over note and comment text. Read every credible candidate's title, notes (`include_details=true` or `timelens_get_plan_item`), and comments (`timelens_list_task_comments`) before selecting or abstaining.
- Choose the task whose title, notes, or comments directly describe the deliverable. Prefer an exact title, then the same deliverable in notes/comments, then the named surface and outcome. Recency only breaks ties between equally relevant tasks. Never default to a broad product task, incidental keyword overlap, or a task used earlier in the chat. Re-check relevance before each comment; keep the same task for the same work chunk unless a better direct match is found.
- On each new user instruction, pull the confidently matched open task to the user's local today if necessary. First read its full details and comments, then preview `timelens_move_plan_item` with `dry_run=true`. Verify the same ID, section, notes, links, comments, assignee, relationships, and existing history are retained; only the scheduled date and appended schedule history may change. Move the existing item, never recreate it. Re-read details and comments after moving and compare them before commenting. Never move an ambiguous match or reopen a completed task just to log work.
- If any preservation check fails, stop TimeLens mutations and record the suspected or confirmed data-loss incident in `docs/known-bugs/` and `docs/agent/session-handover.md` (or the repository's established incident/handover files). Report it and continue independent authorized work where safe.
- Before beginning the requested work, post the user's instruction using `timelens_add_task_comment`, beginning `Prompt before work:`. Include follow-up instructions and remove secrets, tokens, and raw personal data. Write comments in plain text, using `- ` bullet lines when useful, without Markdown bold/emphasis.
- After finishing an implementation, change, commit, push, deployment, or other logical work chunk, post one concise 2-3 line close-out on that work's matching task: what was done, which project/environment changed, verification and commit/push state when relevant, and what remains. Do not duplicate a close-out for the same completed chunk. Logging a chunk does not authorize marking the entire task complete.
- After each prompt or close-out comment, tell the user the task title, scheduled date, and link when available. If logging fails, say why; never claim a comment or move succeeded without confirmation.
- If no confident match exists after searching titles, notes, and comments, ask for the user's go-ahead to create a proposed task for local today, with relevant parent/project relationships. Never comment on or move a weak match. Continue independent requested work while waiting; create a task only after approval.
- If TimeLens is unavailable, report that promptly and continue the requested work. Keep a sanitized pending log in the repository's handover when available, and retry when access returns without duplicating comments. Use the connector; a failure does not authorize browser or desktop control.

The user's standing instruction authorizes prompt comments, close-out comments, and preservation-checked moves of confidently matched tasks to today without asking again. Other TimeLens writes, including task creation, still require authorization. Preserve any separately authorized project-specific timer rule; this work-log rule does not itself start timers or authorize deployment, ad spend, task completion, or unrelated changes.
